candidates.rationale: IC decays steadily across the fit window (0.0250 in 2000 to 0.0010 in 2013), concentrated in 2000-02 and 2008 crisis years and nearly gone by the end. The $high-based upper anchor is the most crowding-prone piece (intraday wick, widely-watched Stochastic-style construction). Swapping it for $close removes that noise source, drops fields 3 to 2, and keeps the single-window self-normalization pattern that scored best this round.

Nearest archive rho is 0.780, one point under the reject line, against a factor using raw $close in the same slot. TS_MIN($low,21) tracks close closely for low-volatility names, driving that collision. Swapping MIN for MEAN decorrelates the price anchor while keeping the EPS + 10-day-return pairing that produced this round's top fitness.

This one carries two edge risks at once: archive rho 0.780 against its near-twin 693246746bbdc073, and 3 shared nodes with alpha033 (limit 4) through the CS_RANK(.../$close) chain. Smoothing the price term breaks the exact RANK-DIV-close match and de-syncs from the archive twin, and should also help the lone negative year (2012) by damping single-day close noise.

Dividing by CS_RANK(...) + 1e-8 blows up for whichever name has the single lowest dollar-volume rank each day, an uncontrolled amplification concentrated in illiquid names. That mechanism is a plausible driver of the sign flip in 2013 and the 0.93 stability. Multiplying keeps the same terms but removes the divide-by-near-zero instability.

IC is negative in exactly 2009 and 2010, a textbook regime problem. Raw dollar_volume has a huge cross-sectional range and dominates the product, so the ranking mostly tracks volume magnitude through the crisis-recovery volume spike rather than EPS. Ranking dollar_volume before multiplying follows this round's own finding to rank or demean it rather than combine it raw.

Bare single-quarter ROA is the only component here and is exposed to one-off reporting noise, plausibly behind the 2003 and 2006 negative years. Smoothing over the trailing two reports (126 days, within this round's accepted window range) should stabilize the signal without adding a new field.

Archive rho is 0.779 against plain TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21), and the half-life doesn't halve inside 63 days, both pointing to raw dollar_volume dominating this ratio's cross-sectional order (an Amihud-style illiquidity proxy in disguise). Ranking dollar_volume first follows this round's guidance to rank/demean it before combining, which should cut the collision and the artificially static character of the signal.

Same divide-by-near-zero-rank flaw as 992f173c32687afe: dividing by CS_RANK(TS_MAX($high,21)) + 1e-8 amplifies whichever name has the lowest 21-day high, typically distressed or low-priced names, right when 2001, 2003, and 2009 (this factor's 3 negative years) saw the most extreme moves in that group. Multiplying removes the blowup while keeping the EPS/return(10) pairing intact.

candidates.rationale: This factor has the batch's shortest half-life (3.0 days) and highest turnover (0.273, costing 0.007 of fitness), a matched pair: the signal reshuffles faster than it can be monetized. A short linear decay smooths day-to-day churn, which should lower turnover and lengthen the effective half-life without touching the underlying min/std construction.

Lowest fitness and ICIR in the batch, negative in 2003/2005/2007, and the only factor here using a raw unranked magnitude as its final cross-sectional signal. Raw dollar-volume level is regime-dependent since a few mega-caps dominate the ordering, which explains the instability. Cross-sectional ranking is the standard fix and also pulls this away from the 0.779 collision with 6ba3b1b13c3d6b6a, whose own dollar_volume term is now separately ranked.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Lookback windows approaching 200 days are cutting it close on coverage for this universe and period; the longest window accepted this round was 126 days, so anything beyond that needs an explicit coverage check before proposing.
  2. Piecewise return transforms (clipping to positive-only, or taking absolute value) combined into a ratio at a 21-day window landed just under the cheap-window bar; this shape needs a different window or a simpler transform before resubmitting.
  3. Standalone timing-of-extremum features (where in a long window the min or max occurred) showed almost no signal alone this round; don't resubmit these without pairing them with a stronger co-factor.
  4. The strongest results this round normalized a price or range value by dispersion measured over that same single window rather than mixing two separate windows; favor this self-normalization pattern for price_volume niches over multi-window combinations.
  5. $earnings_per_share combined with a price or return term produced this round's top 3 fitnesses (7.94, 5.04, 3.17) — favor more fundamental x price/volume pairings over pure price/volume ones.
  6. TS_MEAN($return,10) multiplied by a plain price/volume co-factor (high/close ratio, dollar-volume rank, close delta) failed the cheap screen 3 times this round; the same term paired with $earnings_per_share scored 7.94 and 3.17 — prefer a fundamental co-factor for this term over a price/volume one.
  7. Un-ranked return-sum/delta factors over 40+ day windows with no cross-sectional or fundamental anchor made up over half this round's rejections and mostly failed the cheap screen outright (t 0.04-0.43) — wrap in CS_RANK or pair with a fundamental instead of proposing them bare.
  8. TS_CORR($return, $volume, 42) gave this round's weakest signal (t=0.04) — deprioritize return/volume correlation at medium windows.
  9. Multiplying a bounded price ratio by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, ...) caused 2 of 4 correlation rejections because dollar_volume dominates the product — rank or demean dollar_volume before combining rather than multiplying it in raw.
  10. 4 of 19 rejections were archived trees re-proposed with only a changed window constant or an added DELAY/extra-smoothing wrapper — when mutating an archived parent, change the operator or input field, not just the constants.
  11. The fast/price_volume/low niche looks saturated: $close normalized by rolling std/min/max in the 15-63 day band produced this round's weakest accept (0.004, itself near-duplicate of a rejected subtree) plus 2 of 4 correlation rejections — shift search toward the mixed/medium and mixed/slow niches that produced this round's 4 best scores.
  12. CS_DEMEAN'd asset_turnover crossed with a short close-delta, and CS_RANK of a $return win-count, both cleared the bar only modestly (1.85, 0.89) — iterate on these with alternate fundamentals or count windows rather than repeating plain price/volume normalizations.
